decision: Owner decision O2: raise the pinned workspace compiler to Rust 1.97.1 so a later change can adopt durable-authority-state (Rust 1.96) with its redb adapter.
ordering: The proposal, design and tasks gates passed before the toolchain and code changes.

cargo_environment.wrapper: nix print-dev-env path:$PWD environment of the default development shell, a private Cargo target and TMPDIR. The herdr inventory bounds PATH to 4096 bytes, so the final runs used a PATH of the toolchain, cc, python3, pkg-config, cmake and the system profile.

fixture_identity_changes.cause: The corpus declared toolchain 1.88.0; under the flake's cargo 1.97.1 the harness skipped every execution as the observed toolchain differed, failing planned_commands_qualify_their_views.
fixture_identity_changes.source: config/build-input-contracts.ncl re-declares 1.97.1 (request toolchain and the corpus rust-toolchain.toml channel); nickel export to corpus.json; cargo run --example build-input-qualification --execute under cargo 1.97.1 (c980f4866 2026-06-30) and rustc 1.97.1 (8bab26f4f 2026-07-14); expected.json is that receipt without timings and toolchain.observed
fixture_identity_changes.unchanged: every case's planned inputs, view entries, refusals and execution outcomes (alpha passed, beta failed on its undeclared read, three refused cases not run) and the shared edit
fixture_identity_changes.qualified_by: cargo test -p kiln-web-service --features build-input-fixtures --test build_input_qualification (3 passed) and checks.x86_64-linux.build-input-fixtures

remaining: Rerun nix flake check path:$PWD --no-write-lock-file -L at integration; the shared store's garbage collector blocked further flake builds here.
Follow-up: move the Tree-sitter 0.26 pins to 0.27, which needed Rust 1.90.
Follow-up: drop the detect-coding-agent path patch and use registry 0.1.1, which declares Rust 1.91.
Follow-up: re-evaluate bounded-http (Rust 1.96) for the Celld and webhook shells.
non_claims: Rust 1.97.1 is the tested compiler, not a proven minimum.
Separately pinned runtime, browser (1.90.0), fuzz, Octet overlay and vendored workspaces are not requalified by this change.
Historical evidence and dated records that name Rust 1.88 remain as recorded.
